meaning_en: To start a conversation and make people feel comfortable.
sentence: He told a joke to break the ice at the meeting.

meaning_en: To face something unpleasant bravely because it cannot be avoided.
sentence: I hate dentists, but I bit the bullet and went for the check-up.

meaning_en: Very rarely.
sentence: We eat out once in a blue moon.

idiom: Hit the nail on the head
meaning_en: To describe or do something exactly right.
sentence: You hit the nail on the head with that analysis.

meaning_en: Slightly ill or not feeling well.
sentence: I am feeling under the weather, so I will stay home.

idiom: Cost an arm and a leg
meaning_en: To be extremely expensive.
sentence: A new smartphone can cost an arm and a leg.

meaning_en: To reveal a secret.
sentence: Who spilled the beans about the surprise party?

idiom: Let the cat out of the bag
meaning_en: To reveal a secret by accident.
sentence: She let the cat out of the bag about the new job.

meaning_en: To avoid talking about the main issue.
sentence: Stop beating around the bush and tell me the truth.

meaning_en: To work or study late into the night.
sentence: Students burn the midnight oil before exams.

meaning_en: To stop working on something for the day.
sentence: We have finished the report, so let's call it a day.

meaning_en: Unable to choose between two alternatives.
sentence: He was caught between two stools, unable to pick a college.

meaning_en: To do something carelessly or cheaply in order to save time or money.
sentence: The builder cut corners, and the wall cracked within a year.

meaning_en: To lose courage just before doing something.
sentence: He got cold feet and did not attend the interview.

meaning_en: To ignore someone deliberately.
sentence: After the argument, she gave me the cold shoulder.

meaning_en: To go to bed.
sentence: I am tired, so I am going to hit the sack early.

idiom: Kill two birds with one stone
meaning_en: To achieve two aims with a single action.
sentence: By walking to the bank, I killed two birds with one stone.

meaning_en: To lose an opportunity by being too late.
sentence: If you wait any longer, you will miss the boat on this job.

meaning_en: Finally and permanently.
sentence: Let us settle this issue once and for all.

meaning_en: To tease someone by saying something untrue as a joke.
sentence: Are you serious, or are you pulling my leg?

idiom: Put all your eggs in one basket
meaning_en: To rely completely on a single plan or thing.
sentence: Don't put all your eggs in one basket; invest in several areas.

meaning_en: To understand a hidden meaning that is not stated directly.
sentence: If you read between the lines, the letter was a warning.

meaning_en: A general practical guideline based on experience.
sentence: As a rule of thumb, mix one part cement with three parts sand.

meaning_en: To avoid taking a side in an argument.
sentence: During the debate, the minister sat on the fence.

idiom: Take it with a pinch of salt
meaning_en: To not believe something completely.
sentence: Take his promises with a pinch of salt.

idiom: The ball is in your court
meaning_en: It is now your decision or responsibility to act.
sentence: I have sent the proposal; the ball is in your court.

meaning_en: To ignore something wrong on purpose.
sentence: The officer turned a blind eye to the illegal parking.

meaning_en: Secretly and often illegally, such as a payment made in secret.
sentence: Some shops take payment under the table to avoid tax.

meaning_en: Very angry and ready to protest.
sentence: Parents were up in arms over the new fee.

meaning_en: A search that is pointless or unlikely to succeed.
sentence: Looking for that old file was a wild goose chase.

meaning_en: Something very easy to do.
sentence: The exam was a piece of cake for her.

meaning_en: To make a bad situation worse.
sentence: His rude comment only added fuel to the fire.

meaning_en: At the very last moment.
sentence: The application was submitted at the eleventh hour.

meaning_en: To reveal or make known.
sentence: The investigation brought the fraud to light.

meaning_en: To destroy relations so that one cannot go back.
sentence: If you insult your boss, you may burn your bridges.

meaning_en: By any means, fair or unfair.
sentence: He was determined to win the seat by hook or by crook.

meaning_en: A person who is very similar to a parent.
sentence: Her son is a chip off the old block; he loves music too.

meaning_en: A person who argues the opposite side to test an idea.
sentence: I will play devil's advocate and argue against the plan.

meaning_en: To accept the consequences of one's actions.
sentence: He broke the rule, so now he must face the music.

meaning_en: To become uncontrollable.
sentence: The crowd got out of hand after the match.

meaning_en: To become very angry.
sentence: Dad hit the roof when he saw the broken window.

meaning_en: In the same difficult situation as others.
sentence: We are all in the same boat, so let's help each other.

meaning_en: To watch carefully.
sentence: Please keep an eye on the children while I am away.

meaning_en: A situation where everyone has equal opportunities.
sentence: The new rules give small companies a level playing field.

meaning_en: To earn just enough money to pay for necessities.
sentence: With a small salary, she struggles to make ends meet.

meaning_en: Alert, quick and efficient.
sentence: The new clerk is really on the ball.

meaning_en: To pay far more than something is worth.
sentence: We paid through the nose for the last-minute tickets.

meaning_en: To reveal one's real character or intentions.
sentence: Under pressure, he showed his true colours.

meaning_en: Said when the person we were talking about arrives.
sentence: Speak of the devil; here comes Ravi now.

meaning_en: To be deeply affected by something someone said.
sentence: She took the criticism to heart and improved her work.

meaning_en: The final problem that makes one's patience end.
sentence: Losing my wallet was the last straw after a bad week.

meaning_en: Achieved or gained, often experience.
sentence: He has five years of teaching under his belt.

meaning_en: Past events that no longer matter.
sentence: Our old quarrel is water under the bridge.

meaning_en: A person who spoils others' fun.
sentence: Don't be a wet blanket; come and enjoy the party.

meaning_en: To give up.
sentence: Don't throw in the towel; you are almost there.

meaning_en: To study hard.
sentence: I must hit the books if I want to pass.

meaning_en: A person in an unfamiliar or uncomfortable situation.
sentence: At the formal dinner, I felt like a fish out of water.

meaning_en: To wait patiently without taking action.
sentence: The bus is late, so sit tight for a few minutes.

meaning_en: Something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good.
sentence: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise; I found a better one.
